name: Valentina Jiang
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember handing back a sealed letter without asking what was in it.” People around the public road outside the Port of Asphalt know Valentina by a small Thursday habit. Valentina can recognize shift change by the lull between two groups of walkers.
voice: I heard her say enough in the hallway. I walked her out and saved the father's letter for a day she chooses.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a narrow-striped sweater and a thin silver ring worn on a cord. Valentina has a round face with a pronounced chin, with a center part and straight chestnut hair. Valentina starts to lift a hand, then waits to be invited to speak during a conversation.
personality: Likes beautiful, unnecessary things and gets cross with people who mistake poverty for a lack of taste. Valentina takes longer choosing a cheap birthday card than an expensive coat.
agenda: To deliver the letter only when it is wanted.
family: Lola Vidal is Valentina’s cousin raised in the same household. Valentina brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. Lola makes room at the table. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *Laundry for a stranger*, Lola says, “I use the linen round to keep an eye on three houses.”
connections: Charles Stone. The paid carer and the person holding the letter agree that nobody's frailty requires a forced answer.

reactions.situation: The father offers a letter instead of speaking
reactions.response: Valentina asks whether the daughter wants to take the letter now or leave it closed for another day.
